$comment: Three leather wraps round the throat with a shallow X crossing the front,
read off ref/views/body_2.png and ref/views/head_1.png.
ROUND 2.  Re-measured on the front panel with the metre grid (743.44 px/m,
centreline 195 px).  The wraps' centres are y = 1.4385, 1.4545 and 1.4685
and each is ~9 mm tall, so the stack runs 1.4335..1.4735 -- 40 mm, not the
45 mm round 1 built.  Its half-width there is 0.047 (the dark run at
y = 1.450 is -0.048..+0.046) against a bare neck of 0.044 just above it, so
the leather is only ~3 mm proud and `thickness` must stay small.
At round 1's voxelScale 0.5 -- a 5.3 mm voxel -- the three wraps and the X
fused into one dark blob: the gaps between wraps are 4..6 mm, i.e. under
one voxel.  0.38 (a 4.0 mm voxel) is what lets the gaps read, and it is the
cheapest place on the character to spend triangles because the choker is
small.  The choker was also invisible in round 1 -- it baked inside a 137 mm
ball body.ts had at the throat -- which body.json's measured `yoke` has
since fixed; it is now the outermost surface at the neck.
neck* mirrors head.json's neck column extended down to y = 1.420, which is
the same column body.json's yoke now carries (r 0.0435 at 1.420 tapering to
0.040 at 1.525).  neckInset sinks every piece 6 mm into it so the shell is
13 mm thick and survives the voxel; only the outer 5-9 mm shows.
The top's neck straps pass UNDER this stack: top.json thins their standoff
to 5.8 mm above y = 1.430 so their outer radius, 0.0488, clears the lowest
wrap's 0.0499.  If `gap` or `thickness` here drop, top.neckThinBy has to
grow to match or the strap's cut end pokes through the leather.
